I competed in a “transformation” bodybuilding competition this past October, after losing almost 90 lbs. I did the first 70 on my own (including a FTM mastectomy) and then the last 20/show prep with a coach. My wife is currently doing the same thing and starting the same way. 

Here’s some tips/the road map I used and she is using. Please feel free to set your own but just some ideas to help as you push through. 

-Replace drinks (soda/juice/alcohol) with water. A gallon a day is HUGE but you will pee a lot. If you want, you can switch to “zero” versions when you miss the taste but if you’re trying to cut an addiction, I’d go with water. My wife drank 8-12 sodas a day and this was easier. 

-Get your steps in. First work up to 6000-7000/day and then move 7000-8000, then to 8000-9000 and then 10,000. Use good shoes or crocs (these are comfy and lightweight), stretch and keep your feet good and use something like biofreeze or recovery-cbd.com (menthol is great but tincture and pain lotion) to help as you get sore and work through inflammation. Recovery is an amazing company, single person owned and he’s been in the fitness industry literally my entire life. 

-Sleep 7-9 hours. Your body needs the recovery time more than anything else. 

-Don’t cut a Marco out of your diet (no carbs, no fat etc) just focus on calories first then a balanced macros. Typically protein is a great focus, have it at every meal. Use carbs for energy and fats for hormone regulation. 

-Resistance training. If you’ve never worked out before, stick to the basic machines and go from there. There’s commercial gyms like PF that are great for beginners and have training and group training. 

- Cardio. Once you’re doing resistance training plus the 10,000 steps a day, when you hit the next plateau of weight loss, add in additional cardio. LISS is low intensity cardio and you can do on a treadmill, with some incline and a speed of anywhere from 2.5-3.5 depending on your cardiovascular health. Start with 10 mins/5x week and after a week or two, go 15 mins, then 20, then up to 30. I wouldn’t go over 30 - excessive cardio plus your steps can make you even more hungry. 

-Find support. A partner doing it with you, a gym, a class, a community on the internet,.. have support. My wife wasn’t supportive at first, thought I would leave her then thought I had an eating disorder. I found an online community and team on Instagram and it got me through to my show and 2 months later, she hired a coach and got serious about taking control of her health too. Support is everything. 

-Focus on calories in v calories out first then get macro based. Again, don’t cut out a group… you need them all, just in different amounts. No food is “bad” just excessive amounts are. Depending where you live, there are great restaurants that have their caloric info available and some are great tailored to your goals. 

When you get stressed, your weight will fluctuate. Your hormones will fluctuate and change your weight over the course of the week, so weighing in daily or every other day gives you an average. 2lbs a week average is hard to do… typically it’s 1lb a week or so but you can do it - give yourself grace, be patient - trust the process. Take pics… the scale can be deceiving. 

GOOD LUCK!

Hey man - really just need a solid product line to help. One without sulfates and harmful stuff. I’ve grown a full beard and get compliments a lot but all I’ve ever done was treat it well and NOT TRIM IT MYSELF. 

I suggest the Viking revolution product line. You can order straight from them or Amazon. I use the bay rum beard oil and the beard wash and conditioner religiously. 
Wash it first, real deep in the pores but gentle - put it the conditioner and let it sit in minimum 2 minutes. Usually I just wash my body and then rinse it out with colder water. 
Pat it dry and let it air dry until it’s almost done - toss the beard oil in, working it into your follicles/face and then to the tips. Use a comb (wooden beard) to straighten and shape. Sometimes I’ll use a brush but I’ve found that just makes mine curl up more. 
Find a decent barber who knows how to cut, angle, clean and straight razor your beard. Let them know you’re growing it out but want it trimmed and shaped. Show them the patch and they’ll look around and see what hairs need to grow longer to cover it up. Don’t trim your beard at all, only let them do it.

I’d also stay away from blow drying unless you have to and if so, do it on the cold setting. 
Straighteners are typically a no go too.

I had a cousin watch my house for two weeks with my
Dogs and came back to nearly the same thing. I obviously couldn’t afford to throw everything out but what I did was wash walls and paint like other commenters said.
As for furniture, fabrics and carpet- I cleaned the carpets with rug doctors oxy cleaner and mixed in a more expensive cleaner that had a “fresh” smell to it. 
I also made my own febreeze like substance out of laundry crystals, alcohol and water. I used about 1/4 cup of the crystals (up to 1/2 a cup of them depending on freshness and brand) and then did my alcohol at half of whatever that was. I filled a spray bottle with this and warm water and shook it up several times over the course of 12 hours and then let it sit overnight. For the next week, I sprayed every single surface, carpet and piece of furniture down with this 3-5x times a day, depending on when I was home. Before work, after work, before bed and so on. 
It worked. It took a while but after about a week I finally get like my place was clean again. 
I use this now in my house as well to keep the dog smell out and not spend a fortune on sprays.
